package: W66-01 — real tmux/screen decoding of the hook terminal wrapper
question: Do real multiplexers decode the hook terminal wrapper the product emits?
answer: Yes. A real tmux and a real screen each forward the wrapped OSC 0 so a second tmux parses it and reports the exact pane title, in both source and compiled modes.

method.outer: tmux server with allow-rename on and automatic-rename off; #{pane_title} is the oracle
method.inner: real tmux with allow-passthrough all, or real screen, each running the product formatter
method.delay: 1200 ms after start so the inner client is attached before the effect
method.assertion: outer pane title equals the per-run title; emitted bytes checked for the wrapper prefix

changes.change: three C-6 rows record the completed mux gap
lifecycle hooks row records mux verification and delivery disposition

delivery.contract: append hook_terminal, then write the TTY; resume keeps records without replay
delivery.exactlyOnce: not provable; the TTY has no acknowledgment channel

residuals: Zellij detection exists in the recovered K3t body but is not ported.
The first full-suite run at concurrency 4 timed out in unrelated worktree cases under host load; the isolated concurrency-2 rerun passed.
Screen 4.00.03 forwards the doubled ESC verbatim; decoding depends on the parser tolerating the prefix ESC ESC.
